name: 1 Leg Box Squat
description: This exercise requires a sturdy box or a chair. Simple stand ~6 inches in front of it and balance yourself on one leg. From here, begin squatting down in a smooth controlled motion while keeping your other leg straight out in front of you for balance. Slowly sit down on the box, pause for a 1 count and push back up with the working leg, while never letting your other leg touch the ground.

name: 1-Arm Half-Kneeling Lat Pulldown
description: Attach a D-Handle to a high pully. And use your lat muscles to pull the weight single handedly.

name: 1/2 Kneeling Thoracic Rotation
description: Begin in a half kneeling position with the leg away from the wall stabilized against the wall with a ball. With both hands directly in front of you, rotate one arm open attempting to reach the wall behind you. Exhale as you rotate, inhale as you return to neutral and repeat.

name: 2 Handed Kettlebell Swing
description: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, the kettlebell on the floor about 20-30 cm in front of your toes. Hinge at the hips with a slight bend in the knees and a flat back, and grip the handle with both hands. Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, then drive your hips forward explosively so that it swings forward and up to chest or shoulder height (Russian style, not overhead). Your arms stay straight and relaxed, the power comes from the hips. Let the kettlebell swing back down, hinge again as it passes between your legs and go straight into the next rep.

name: 3/4 Sit-Up
description: Lie down on the floor and secure your feet. Your legs should be bent at the knees. Place your hands behind or to the side of your head. You will begin with your back on the ground. This will be your starting position. Flex your hips and spine to raise your torso toward your knees. At the top of the contraction your torso should be perpendicular to the ground. Reverse the motion, going only ¾ of the way down. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: 3008 Abdominal Crunch
description: This is especially for the gym80 device 3008 Abdominal Crunch.

name: 3D Lunge Warmup
description: As a warmup, use light dumbbells, one in each hand. Lunge in alternating directions, forward, sideways, backwards and 45 degree angles.

name: 4-Count Burpees
description: Starting position: Stand straight, feet hip-width apart. Steps: Squat low and support yourself on the floor with your hands between the knees and in front of your feet, your back straight. Keeping your hands on the floor, jump your legs backward into high plank position. Jump your feet forward to return to the squat position. Repeat.

name: 45° Lateral Raises
description: Dumbbell raise at an angle halfway between a front raise and a lateral raise.

name: 45° Side Bend
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and your arms extended straight down by your sides. With your back straight and your core engaged, With control bend your torso to one side, lowering your hand toward your knee. Stand or sit tall with the pelvis facing forward. Bend sideways through the waist without twisting or letting the hips shift. Let the side of the trunk work; do not twist or shift the hips. Bring the weight or body back to its starting position without rushing.

name: 90/90 Breathing
description: Controlled breathing drill performed in a 90/90 position to encourage rib, abdominal, and pelvic coordination.

name: 90/90 Hamstring
description: Lie on your back, with one leg extended straight out. With the other leg, bend the hip and knee to 90 degrees. You may brace your leg with your hands if necessary. This will be your starting position. Extend your leg straight into the air, pausing briefly at the top. Return the leg to the starting position. Repeat for 10-20 repetitions, and then switch to the other leg.

name: 90/90 Hip Switches
description: Sit on the floor with one leg bent at 90 degrees in front of you and the other leg bent at 90 degrees out to the side, so that the rear shin is parallel to the front shin. Keep your torso upright and, if possible, your hands off the floor. Rotate both knees over to the other side so that the legs swap positions and you arrive in the same 90/90 position facing the opposite way. Move slowly and under control, keeping the feet in contact with the floor, and alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions. Mobility drill for internal and external rotation of the hips.

name: Ab Wheel
description: Starting Position: Kneel on the floor with the ab wheel in front of you. Grip the Wheel: Hold the handles firmly. Roll Out: Slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your body while keeping your core tight. Return: Pull the wheel back towards your knees, maintaining tension in your core.

name: Abdominal Crunch
description: The Abdominal Crunch is a classic core isolation exercise performed on the floor or a mat. Unlike a full sit-up, it involves a smaller range of motion where you only lift your shoulders and upper back off the ground, keeping your lower back pressed firmly against the floor.

name: Abdominal Draw-In
description: Lie on your back with knees bent. Gently pull your belly button toward your spine without moving your hips or holding your breath.

name: Abduction While Standing
description: Training a stable stance, predominantly on one leg, is crucial for both sides. On the one hand, it prevents discomfort and, on the other, it establishes a stable foundation. The practitioner assumes the usual standing position and, with a stable upper body, attempts to repeatedly lift the unloaded leg, bend it at the hip and knee, and then lower it again. The movement is also repeated on the other side. The exercise trains the stability of the hip-surrounding muscles.

name: Active Hang
description: A static hold from a pull-up bar with straight elbows and actively depressed, stabilized shoulders. Grip a secure bar and let your body hang under control. Keep your elbows straight and gently draw your shoulders down, away from your ears. Maintain this active shoulder position without pulling up, swinging, or repeatedly moving the shoulder blades. Hold for up to 30 seconds. Stop earlier if your grip opens, shoulder control deteriorates, or pain occurs. Record actual seconds, grip, and any assistance used. This is distinct from a relaxed passive dead hang or a moving scapular pull-up.

name: Adductor
description: Lie face down with one leg on a foam roll. Rotate the leg so that the foam roll contacts against your inner thigh. Shift as much weight onto the foam roll as can be tolerated. While trying to relax the muscles if the inner thigh, roll over the foam between your hip and knee, holding points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat with the other leg.

name: Adductor Rock Backs
description: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Extend one leg straight out to the side with the foot flat on the floor and the toes pointing forward. Keep your back flat and slowly push your hips back towards the heel of the kneeling leg until you feel a stretch along the inside of the extended leg. Pause briefly, then return to the starting position. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching legs. Mobility exercise for the adductors and the hips.

name: Adductor/Groin
description: Lie on your back with your feet raised towards the ceiling. Have your partner hold your feet or ankles. Abduct your legs as far as you can. This will be your starting position. Attempt to squeeze your legs together for 10 or more seconds, while your partner prevents you from doing so. Now, relax the muscles in your legs as your partner pushes your feet apart, stretching as far as is comfortable for you. Be sure to let your partner know when the stretch is adequate to prevent overstretching or injury.

name: All Fours Quad Stretch
description: Start off on your hands and knees, then lift your leg off the floor and hold the foot with your hand. Use your hand to hold the foot or ankle, keeping the knee fully flexed, stretching the quadriceps and hip flexors. Focus on extending your hips, thrusting them towards the floor. Hold for 10-20 seconds and then switch sides.

name: All Fours Squad Stretch
description: Get onto hands and knees with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips. Reach one leg straight back, keeping your knee bent and your foot flexed. Settle into the starting position and take an easy breath before moving deeper. Ease toward the stretch until you feel mild tension; keep breathing and avoid bouncing. Stay in a mild stretch rather than pulling farther with momentum. Hold the position with steady breathing, then release gently; repeat on the other side if needed.

name: Alternate Back Lunges
description: The posterior muscles of the buttocks, hamstrings, soleus and gastrocnemius are trained more

name: Alternate Hammer Curl
description: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso. The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position. While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in. Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition. Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Alternate Heel Touchers
description: Lie on the floor with the knees bent and the feet on the floor around 18-24 inches apart. Your arms should be extended by your side. This will be your starting position. Crunch over your torso forward and up about 3-4 inches to the right side and touch your right heel as you hold the contraction for a second. Exhale while performing this movement. Now go back slowly to the starting position as you inhale. Now crunch over your torso forward and up around 3-4 inches to the left side and touch your left heel as you hold the contraction for a second. Exhale while performing this movement and then go back to the starting position as you inhale. Now that both heels have been touched, that is considered 1 repetition. Continue alternating sides in this manner until all prescribed repetitions are done.

name: Alternate Incline Dumbbell Curl
description: Sit down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. Tip: Keep the elbows close to the torso.This will be your starting position. While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. As you do so, rotate the hand so that the palm is facing up. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Slowly begin to bring the dumbbell back to starting position as your breathe in. Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition. Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Alternate Lateral Pulldown
description: Take a seat on the cable machine with your back straight and feet planted. Hold the handles with palms facing down, just beyond shoulder width. Sit tall and set the shoulders before drawing the handle down. Pull the handle down by driving your elbows toward your ribs; keep your torso steady. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Let the handle rise steadily until the arms are long, then reset the shoulders; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
description: Assume a comfortable stance with one foot slightly in front of the other. Begin by pushing off with the front leg, driving the opposite knee forward and as high as possible before landing. Attempt to cover as much distance to each side with each bound. It may help to use a line on the ground to guage distance from side to side. Repeat the sequence with the other leg.

name: Alternate Walking
description: 1m30s of walking (~4.5 km/h) to 30 s of jog (7 km/h) and repeat

name: Alternating Bicep Curls
description: Starting position: Start standing up with dumbbells in each hand, your back straight and feet hip-width apart. Your arms should be relaxed, pointing down. Your knees should be slightly bent, your abs contracted, and your shoulders down. Steps: Bend one arm at the elbow, bringing the dumbbell up to your shoulder. Your upper arm should remain motionless during this movement. Bring the dumbbell back down until your arm is in its original relaxed position. Repeat, switching arms.

name: Alternating Cable Shoulder Press
description: Move the cables to the bottom of the tower and select an appropriate weight. Grasp the cables and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This will be your starting position. Keeping your head and chest up, extend through the elbow to press one side directly over head. After pausing at the top, return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.

name: Alternating Deltoid Raise
description: In a standing position, hold a pair of dumbbells at your side. Keeping your elbows slightly bent, raise the weights directly in front of you to shoulder height, avoiding any swinging or cheating. Return the weights to your side. On the next repetition, raise the weights laterally, raising them out to your side to about shoulder height. Return the weights to the starting position and continue alternating to the front and side.

name: Alternating Dumbbell Hammer Curl
description: Stand with your knees slightly bent and your back straight. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, using a neutral grip at your sides.

name: Alternating High Cable Row
description: Start by putting the attachment in a high position on the cable station and step back about 1m from the attachment. Grab the cable pulley handle in your left hand at about head height with your elbow slightly bent. Step back with your left foot. Pull your elbow joint in toward the torso twisting slightly and perform a single-arm row. Engage the lats as you twist. Return to the starting position with cable pulley and left foot and grab the cable pulley handle in the right hand. Repeat this motion on the opposite side with your right foot stepped back.

name: Alternating Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: Take a seat on a bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards, and raise them to shoulder height. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Alternative DB Gorilla Rows
description: Slightly bent down and knees to mimic a gorilla position and pull/row up the DBs to the chest. DB stay straight (thumbs pointing up)

name: Ankle Circles
description: Use a sturdy object like a squat rack to hold yourself. Lift the right leg in the air (just around 2 inches from the floor) and perform a circular motion with the big toe. Pretend that you are drawing a big circle with it. Tip: One circle equals 1 repetition. Breathe normally as you perform the movement. When you are done with the right foot, then repeat with the left leg.

name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Rocks
description: Move your knee forward, keeping your heel on the ground. Hold the position for a couple of seconds and return to the starting position.

name: Ankle On The Knee
description: From a lying position, bend your knees and keep your feet on the floor. Place your ankle of one foot on your opposite knee. Grasp the thigh or knee of the bottom leg and pull both of your legs into the chest. Relax your neck and shoulders. Hold for 10-20 seconds and then switch sides.

name: Ankle Roll
description: Sit on the floor and lift one foot off the ground, for example by resting that leg on the other knee. Slowly draw circles with your foot, moving only at the ankle. Do several circles in both directions, then switch feet.

name: Anterior Tibialis-SMR
description: Begin seated on the ground with your legs bent and your feet on the floor. Using a Muscle Roller or a rolling pin, apply pressure to the muscles on the outside of your shins. Work from just below the knee to above the ankle, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat on the other leg.

name: Anti-Gravity Press
description: Place a bar on the ground behind the head of an incline bench. Lay on the bench face down. With a pronated grip, pick the barbell up from the floor. Flex the elbows, performing a reverse curl to bring the bar near your chest. This will be your starting position. To begin, press the barbell out in front of your head by extending your elbows. Keep your arms parallel to the ground throughout the movement. Return to the starting position and repeat to complete the set.

name: Arabesque
description: Take all your weight onto one leg and you're going to maintain that position, keeping your hips and pelvis level the whole time. With your back in a neutral position you want to tilt yourself forward kicking your leg back up and then slowly with your glutes bring yourself back up to neutral.

name: Arch Hang
description: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C995b3KLXS4&t=7s Elbows should stay straight Hold it for time/reps Start at an active hang: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HoE-C85ZlCE Progress towards a 90 degree in your shoulder

name: Archer Pull-Up
description: Begin by hanging from a pull-up bar with palms facing down, just beyond shoulder width. Brace your trunk and pull your shoulder blades down and back. Begin from a controlled hang with the shoulders active rather than slack. Pull your elbows down and bring your upper chest toward the bar without kicking your legs. Avoid swinging the legs to clear the bar. Lower to long arms without dropping suddenly from the top.

name: Archer Push Up
description: Begin in a push-up position with your hands just beyond shoulder width. Reach one arm straight out to the side, parallel to the ground. Brace the abdomen and glutes so the shoulders, hips and ankles move together. Shift toward one hand and bend that elbow while the other arm straightens to the side. Keep the head in line with the spine as the elbows bend. Press back to straight arms, keeping the body line intact.

name: Arm and Neck Stretch
description: Relieves tension in the upper body, especially useful for people with office jobs or prolonged postures.

name: Arm Circles
description: Stand up and extend your arms straight out by the sides. The arms should be parallel to the floor and perpendicular (90-degree angle) to your torso. This will be your starting position. Slowly start to make circles of about 1 foot in diameter with each outstretched arm. Breathe normally as you perform the movement. Continue the circular motion of the outstretched arms for about ten seconds. Then reverse the movement, going the opposite direction.

name: Arm Raises (T/Y/I)
description: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, core engaged, and arms relaxed at your sides. From this position, perform three different arm raises to target the shoulders and upper back: T Raise: Lift your arms straight out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, forming a “T” shape. Y Raise: Lift your arms upward at about a 45° angle from your body to form a “Y” shape. I Raise: Raise your arms straight overhead, close together, forming an “I” shape. Maintain a neutral spine, avoid arching your lower back, and move slowly with control. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together and keeping your shoulders down away from your ears.

name: Arm Slingers Hanging Bent Knee Legs
description: Suspend yourself from a pull-up bar with your arms straight and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle. Brace your trunk and lift your knees toward your chest, bringing them as close to your elbows as possible. Brace the abdomen and keep the shoulders anchored to the support. Lift your legs by bracing your trunk and moving at the hips rather than swinging. Slow the legs before they pull the lower back out of position. Lower the legs slowly without swinging or losing your trunk position.

name: Arm Slingers Hanging Straight-Legs
description: Suspend yourself from a pull-up bar with your arms straight and your legs straight down. Brace your trunk and lift your legs up in front of you until they are parallel to the ground. Brace the abdomen and keep the shoulders anchored to the support. Lift your legs by bracing your trunk and moving at the hips rather than swinging. Slow the legs before they pull the lower back out of position. Lower the legs slowly without swinging or losing your trunk position.

name: Arms Apart Circular Toe Touch
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and arms extended to the sides. With your legs straight, bend forward at the waist and reach down toward your toes with your right hand. Soften the knees and let the hips start the fold. Fold forward from the hips and let your hands travel toward your feet without forcing the reach. Keep the movement controlled throughout the range. Hold briefly at a comfortable depth, then rise by extending the hips.

name: Arms Overhead Full Sit-Up
description: Settle onto your back with your knees bent and feet planted. Reach your arms overhead, keeping them straight. Set the pelvis and keep the neck relaxed before curling upward. Curl your rib cage toward your pelvis, letting the abdominals move the torso. Leave a little space between the chin and chest; keep the movement in the torso. Lower the shoulders or torso with control before the next curl.

name: Arnold Shoulder Press
description: Sit on a bench with your back supported. Hold a pair of dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you and elbows in front of your body. Press the dumbbells overhead while rotating your hands, so that your palms face forward at the top. Stop just before your elbows lock out. Reverse the movement under control: lower the dumbbells and turn your palms back towards you until you are in the starting position again. As shown here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vj2w851ZHRM

name: Assisted Chin-Ups
description: Chin-ups with machine assistance (counterweights)

name: Assisted Hanging Knee Raise with Throw Down
description: Suspend yourself from a pull-up bar with your arms straight and your palms turned away from you. Brace your trunk and lift your knees toward your chest, keeping your legs together. Brace the abdomen and keep the shoulders anchored to the support. Lift your legs by bracing your trunk and moving at the hips rather than swinging. Slow the legs before they pull the lower back out of position. Lower the legs slowly without swinging or losing your trunk position.

name: Assisted Lying Calves Stretch
description: Settle onto your back with your legs extended. Before moving, bend one knee and place your foot flat on the ground. Settle into the starting position and take an easy breath before moving deeper. Ease toward the stretch until you feel mild tension; keep breathing and avoid bouncing. Stay in a mild stretch rather than pulling farther with momentum. Hold the position with steady breathing, then release gently; repeat on the other side if needed.

name: Assisted Lying Glutes Stretch
description: Settle onto your back with your legs extended. Before moving, bend your right knee and place your right ankle on your left thigh, just above the knee. Settle into the starting position and take an easy breath before moving deeper. Ease toward the stretch until you feel mild tension; keep breathing and avoid bouncing. Stay in a mild stretch rather than pulling farther with momentum. Hold the position with steady breathing, then release gently; repeat on the other side if needed.

name: Assisted Lying Gluteus and Piriformis Stretch
description: Settle onto your back with your legs extended. Before moving, bend your right knee and place your right ankle on your left thigh, just above the knee. Settle into the starting position and take an easy breath before moving deeper. Ease toward the stretch until you feel mild tension; keep breathing and avoid bouncing. Stay in a mild stretch rather than pulling farther with momentum. Hold the position with steady breathing, then release gently; repeat on the other side if needed.

name: Assisted Lying Leg Raise with Throw Down
description: Settle onto your back with your legs extended and your arms by your sides. Set your hands under your glutes for support. Brace the abdomen and keep the shoulders anchored to the support. Lift your legs by bracing your trunk and moving at the hips rather than swinging. Slow the legs before they pull the lower back out of position. Lower the legs slowly without swinging or losing your trunk position.

name: Assisted Motion Russian Twist
description: Take a seat on the ground with your knees bent and feet planted. Take hold of the medicine ball with both hands ahead of your chest. Set the pelvis and make the turn through the rib cage. Turn through the torso while the hips and lower body stay as steady as the setup allows. Keep the turn smooth instead of throwing the arms across the body. Return through center before turning to the other side.

name: Assisted Parallel Close-Grip Pull-Up
description: Set the machine to your desired weight and height. Set your hands on the parallel bars with a close grip, palms facing each other. Begin from a controlled hang with the shoulders active rather than slack. Pull your elbows down and bring your upper chest toward the bar without kicking your legs. Avoid swinging the legs to clear the bar. Lower to long arms without dropping suddenly from the top.

name: Assisted Prone Hamstring
description: Position yourself face down on a mat or bench with your legs straight. Ask a partner to help or use a resistance band to secure your ankles. Line the knees up with the machine or bench edge before starting the curl. Bend your knees to draw the pad toward you without lifting your hips from the support. Keep the hips still while the knees bend. Ease back to the start before repeating.

name: Assisted Prone Lying Quads Stretch
description: Position yourself face down on the ground with your legs extended. Before moving, bend your left knee and reach back with your left hand to grab your left foot or ankle. Settle into the starting position and take an easy breath before moving deeper. Ease toward the stretch until you feel mild tension; keep breathing and avoid bouncing. Stay in a mild stretch rather than pulling farther with momentum. Hold the position with steady breathing, then release gently; repeat on the other side if needed.

name: Assisted Prone Rectus Femoris Stretch
description: Position yourself face down on the ground with your legs straight. Before moving, bend your right knee and reach back with your right hand to grab your right foot or ankle. Settle into the starting position and take an easy breath before moving deeper. Ease toward the stretch until you feel mild tension; keep breathing and avoid bouncing. Stay in a mild stretch rather than pulling farther with momentum. Hold the position with steady breathing, then release gently; repeat on the other side if needed.

name: Assisted Seated Pectoralis Major Stretch with Stability Ball
description: Take a seat on a stability ball with your feet planted and your back straight. Take a stability ball with both hands and extend your arms straight out in front of you. Settle into the starting position and take an easy breath before moving deeper. Ease toward the stretch until you feel mild tension; keep breathing and avoid bouncing. Keep the ball steady and use the feet to manage your balance. Hold the position with steady breathing, then release gently; repeat on the other side if needed.

name: Assisted Side-Lying Adductor Stretch
description: Settle onto your side with your legs straight and stacked on top of each other. Before moving, bend your bottom leg slightly for stability. Settle into the starting position and take an easy breath before moving deeper. Ease toward the stretch until you feel mild tension; keep breathing and avoid bouncing. Stay in a mild stretch rather than pulling farther with momentum. Hold the position with steady breathing, then release gently; repeat on the other side if needed.

name: Assisted Sit-Up
description: Sit at the bench edge, or ask a partner to secure your feet. Settle onto your back with your knees bent and feet planted. Set the pelvis and keep the neck relaxed before curling upward. Curl your rib cage toward your pelvis, letting the abdominals move the torso. Leave a little space between the chin and chest; keep the movement in the torso. Lower the shoulders or torso with control before the next curl.

name: Assisted Standing Chin-Up
description: Set the machine to your desired assistance level. Step onto the foot platform and grip the handles with palms facing down, just beyond shoulder width. Begin from a controlled hang with the shoulders active rather than slack. Pull your elbows down and bring your upper chest toward the bar without kicking your legs. Avoid swinging the legs to clear the bar. Lower to long arms without dropping suddenly from the top.

name: Assisted Standing Triceps Extension (with Towel)
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold a towel with both hands behind your head. Hold your elbows near your ears and your upper arms stationary. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Keep the upper arms steady while the forearms travel. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep.

name: Assisted Triceps Dip (kneeling)
description: Set the machine to your desired weight and height. Get down on the pad facing the machine, with your hands gripping the handles. Set the shoulders down and keep the elbows pointed mostly behind you. Bend the elbows to lower between the supports; stop at a comfortable shoulder depth. Choose a depth that lets the shoulders stay comfortable. Press through the hands to rise, then reset the shoulders before another rep.

name: Assisted Wide-Grip Chest Dip (kneeling)
description: Set the machine to your desired height and secure your knees on the pad. Hold the handles with a wide grip and keep your elbows soft. Set the shoulders down and keep the elbows pointed mostly behind you. Bend the elbows to lower between the supports; stop at a comfortable shoulder depth. Choose a depth that lets the shoulders stay comfortable. Press through the hands to rise, then reset the shoulders before another rep.

name: Astride Jumps
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width. Before moving, bend your knees and lower your body into a squat position. Bend the hips and knees slightly to load the jump. Load the legs with a small bend, then drive through the floor and land softly. Land with bent hips and knees and let the feet absorb the impact. Absorb the landing through the hips and knees before repeating.

name: Atlas Stone Trainer
description: This trainer is effective for developing Atlas Stone strength for those who don't have access to stones, and are typically made from bar ends or heavy pipe. Begin by loading the desired weight onto the bar. Straddle the weight, wrapping your arms around the implement, bending at the hips. Begin by pulling the weight up past the knees, extending through the hips. As the weight clears the knees, it can be lapped by resting it on your thighs and sitting back, hugging it tightly to your chest. Finish the movement by extending through your hips and knees to raise the weight as high as possible. The weight can be returned to the lap or to the ground for successive repetitions.

name: Atlas Stones
description: Begin with the atlas stone between your feet. Bend at the hips to wrap your arms vertically around the Atlas Stone, attempting to get your fingers underneath the stone. Many stones will have a small flat portion on the bottom, which will make the stone easier to hold. Pulling the stone into your torso, drive through the back half of your feet to pull the stone from the ground. As the stone passes the knees, lap it by sitting backward, pulling the stone on top of your thighs. Sit low, getting the stone high onto your chest as you change your grip to reach over the stone. Stand, driving through with your hips. Close distance to the loading platform, and lean back, extending the hips to get the stone as high as possible.

name: Australian Pull-Ups
description: Lie down under a high bar or suspension bar, positioned at an appropriate height. Position yourself on your back under the bar, gripping the bar with a supinated grip (palms facing you). Adjust your position so that your body is aligned straight from head to toe. Arms should be fully extended, shoulders stabilized, and legs aligned with the rest of the body. Bend your elbows and pull your chest towards the bar, contracting your back muscles. Imagine you're trying to bring your shoulder blades together. Hold the contraction at the top of the movement for a moment to maximize muscle activation. Slowly return to the starting position, extending your elbows.

name: Axe Hold
description: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and raise your straight arms out to the sides to shoulder height. Hold this position for as long as you can.

name: Axle Deadlift
description: Approach the bar so that it is centered over your feet. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hip to grip the bar at shoulder width, allowing your shoulder blades to protract. Typically, you would use an over/under grip. With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees until your shins contact the bar. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward. After the bar passes the knees, aggressively pull the bar back, pulling your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward into the bar. Lower the bar by bending at the hips and guiding it to the floor.

name: Back and Forth Step
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width. Move forward with your right foot, bending your knee and lowering your body into a lunge position. Start at a pace that lets the feet and arms move in sync. Move at a repeatable pace, keeping the motion smooth and your breathing steady. Keep the pattern repeatable as speed increases. Keep the rhythm for the planned interval, slowing if your form starts to slip.

name: Back Bridge
description: Lie on the floor with your back resting on the floor and your legs bent, feet flat on the floor, leaving about 20 cm between your feet and your buttocks. Your hands remain flat on the floor, pressed against your ears, with your fingers pointing toward your toes. Your elbows are bent and pointing toward the ceiling. This is the starting position. Now push your hips as high as you can, raising your body off the floor, and continue pushing through your hands, extending your elbows and knees, until your back is fully arched (lumbar bridge). Your head also comes off the floor and should be level with your elbows, looking back. This is the final position. The descent should be slow and controlled. Your spine should be in a convex curve. It's not good to lift your back off the floor; it should remain straight. It should be well rounded. You'll also notice a feeling of increased oxygenation in your back. After lifting off the floor, your hips should be very high, even above the level of your head. Your arms and legs should remain straight. It seems easy, but it requires a good level of flexibility. Breathing should be deep. This posture stretches the rib cage and puts pressure on the diaphragm. If the posture is performed correctly, breathing will be perfect. Never hold your breath during the exercise.

name: Back Extension on Exercise Ball
description: Set the stability ball on the ground and Position yourself face down on top of it, with your hips resting on the ball and your feet against a wall or other stable surface. Set your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest. Secure the hips and feet on the support before lifting. Raise your torso or legs until they line up with your body, without arching sharply at the lower back. Keep the ball steady and use the feet to manage your balance. Return along the same path at a controlled pace.

name: Back Flyes - With Bands
description: Run a band around a stationary post like that of a squat rack. Grab the band by the handles and stand back so that the tension in the band rises. Extend and lift the arms straight in front of you. Tip: Your arms should be straight and parallel to the floor while perpendicular to your torso. Your feet should be firmly planted on the floor spread at shoulder width. This will be your starting position. As you exhale, move your arms to the sides and back. Keep your arms extended and parallel to the floor. Continue the movement until the arms are extended to your sides. After a pause, go back to the original position as you inhale. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Back Lever
description: Begin by hanging from a pull-up bar with palms facing down, hands just beyond shoulder width. Brace your trunk and pull your shoulder blades down and back. Brace the abdomen and find a position you can maintain without holding your breath. Brace your midsection and hold the position while breathing normally. Keep breathing steadily as you maintain the same body line. Keep the shape for the planned time, then come out of it with control.

name: Back Neck Stretch
description: Starting position: Sit upright on a chair or a firm pillow. Steps: Breathe out and tilt your head forward, chin to chest, putting hands behind your head. Use your hands to pull your head down lightly and press against your hands with your head to balance out the force. Hold for a bit. Relax your arms and head, opening up a bit with your shoulders. Keep repeating this from step 2 onward.

name: Back Pec Stretch
description: Stand tall and set your feet about shoulder width. Reach your arms straight out in front of you, parallel to the ground. Settle into the starting position and take an easy breath before moving deeper. Ease toward the stretch until you feel mild tension; keep breathing and avoid bouncing. Stay in a mild stretch rather than pulling farther with momentum. Hold the position with steady breathing, then release gently; repeat on the other side if needed.

name: Backward Arm Circles
description: Starting position: Stand tall with your back straight. Steps: Keeping your arms straight, bring them in front of you, raise them over your head, then continue the motion behind your back and down to the initial position. Keep circling your arms as described in step 1.

name: Backward Drag
description: Load a sled with the desired weight, attaching a rope or straps to the sled that you can hold onto. Begin the exercise by moving backwards for a given distance. Leaning back, extend through the legs for short steps to move as quickly as possible.

name: Backward Jump
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width. Before moving, bend your knees slightly and jump backwards, pushing off with both feet. Bend the hips and knees slightly to load the jump. Load the legs with a small bend, then drive through the floor and land softly. Land with bent hips and knees and let the feet absorb the impact. Absorb the landing through the hips and knees before repeating.

name: Backward Medicine Ball Throw
description: This exercise is best done with a partner. If you lack a partner, the ball can be thrown and retrieved or thrown against a wall. Begin standing a few meters in front of your partner, both facing the same direction. Begin holding the ball between your legs. Squat down and then forcefully reverse direction, coming to full extension and you toss the ball over your head to your partner. Your partner can then roll the ball back to you. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

name: Backward Shoulder Rotation
description: Starting position: Sit or stand with your back straight. Steps: Place your hands on your shoulders. Repeatedly rotate both shoulder joints in a circular motion at a moderate pace.

name: Bag Training
description: Bag training improves muscle definition of: deltoids; rear deltoids; triceps; biceps, as well as being a great cardio exercise

name: Balance Board
description: Place a balance board in front of you. Stand up on it and try to balance yourself. Hold the balance for as long as desired.

name: Ball Leg Curl
description: Begin on the floor laying on your back with your feet on top of the ball. Position the ball so that when your legs are extended your ankles are on top of the ball. This will be your starting position. Raise your hips off of the ground, keeping your weight on the shoulder blades and your feet. Flex the knees, pulling the ball as close to you as you can, contracting the hamstrings. After a brief pause, return to the starting position.

name: Ball Slams
description: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, your knees and hips slightly bent, holding the ball in both hands at chest height. Engage your core, and keep a good posture. Extend your knees and drive your hips forward while simultaneously lifting the ball. Aim for being as tall as possible, the ball overhead, arms up, hips slightly forward, and on your toes from the force of your drive. Use your core and arms to slam the medicine ball straight down between your feet with as much force as possible. Press your hips back and bend your knees to further power the slam. Exhale as you slam the ball down. Squat down to pick up the ball from the floor, then immediately move into the next slam by repeating the movement. Repeat for reps or time.

name: Band Alternating V-Up
description: Settle onto your back with your legs straight and your arms extended overhead, holding the band. Tighten your midsection and lift your legs and upper body off the ground simultaneously, reaching your hands toward your toes. Set the pelvis and keep the neck relaxed before curling upward. Raise your straight legs and torso together, reaching toward the feet before lowering under control. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Lower the shoulders or torso with control before the next curl; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Band Assisted Pull-Up
description: Connect the band to a pull-up bar or sturdy anchor point. Step onto the band and grip the bar with your palms turned away from you, hands just beyond shoulder width. Begin from a controlled hang with the shoulders active rather than slack. Pull your elbows down and bring your upper chest toward the bar without kicking your legs. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower to long arms without dropping suddenly from the top.

name: Band Assisted Wheel Rollout
description: Get down on the floor and hold the handles of the band with both hands, palms facing down. Set the band on the ground in front of you and position your hands about shoulder width. Tighten the abdomen and keep the pelvis tucked before the arms reach away. Reach the arms away while keeping your ribs and pelvis aligned; stop before the lower back sags. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Pull back to the start through your shoulders and abdominals, keeping the same body line.

name: Band Bench Press
description: Using a flat bench secure a band under the leg of the bench that is nearest to your head. Once the band is secure, grab it by both handles and lie down on the bench. Extend your arms so that you are holding the band handles in front of you at shoulder width. Once at shoulder width, rotate your wrists forward so that the palms of your hands are facing away from you. This will be your starting position. Bring down the handles slowly until your elbow forms a 90 degree angle. Keep full control at all times. As you breathe out, bring the handles up using your pectoral muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, squeeze your chest, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up. Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions of your training program.

name: Band Bent-Over Hip Extension
description: Secure the band low on a solid anchor. Face the away from the anchor point from a stable stance with feet about shoulder width. Plant the feet and keep the ribs from flaring as the hips prepare to rise. Press through the feet and lift your hips until your torso and thighs line up. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the hips steadily and keep the feet planted for the next lift.

name: Band Bicycle Crunch
description: Settle onto your back with your hands behind your head and your knees bent. Lift your feet off the ground and bring your right knee toward your chest while simultaneously twisting your torso to bring your left elbow toward your right knee. Set the pelvis and keep the neck relaxed before curling upward. Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee as the other leg extends; switch sides in a steady rhythm. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the shoulders or torso with control before the next curl.

name: Band Close-Grip Pulldown
description: Connect the band to a high anchor point, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam. Face the anchor point and grab the band with palms facing up, hands about shoulder width. Sit tall and set the shoulders before drawing the handle down. Pull the handle down by driving your elbows toward your ribs; keep your torso steady. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Let the handle rise steadily until the arms are long, then reset the shoulders.

name: Band Close-Grip Push-Up
description: Set a band around your upper arms, just above the elbows. Get into a push-up position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels. Brace the abdomen and glutes so the shoulders, hips and ankles move together. Bend your elbows to lower your chest while keeping your body in one line. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Press back to straight arms, keeping the body line intact.

name: Band Concentration Curl
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your legs spread apart and your feet planted. Keep one end of the band in your hand and step on the other end with your foot on the same side. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Band Finger Extensions
description: Put a small rubber band around all five fingertips. Spread your fingers and thumb open as wide as possible against the band, hold for a second, then close slowly. This trains the extensor muscles that open the hand and balances heavy gripping, which helps keep the elbows and wrists healthy.

name: Band Fixed Back Close-Grip Pulldown
description: Connect the band to a fixed point above you, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam. Sit down on a bench or chair facing the band, with your feet planted and your knees bent. Sit tall and set the shoulders before drawing the handle down. Pull the handle down by driving your elbows toward your ribs; keep your torso steady. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Let the handle rise steadily until the arms are long, then reset the shoulders.

name: Band Fixed Back Underhand Pulldown
description: Connect the band to a sturdy anchor point above your head. Face the anchor point from a stable stance with feet about shoulder width. Sit tall and set the shoulders before drawing the handle down. Pull the handle down by driving your elbows toward your ribs; keep your torso steady. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Let the handle rise steadily until the arms are long, then reset the shoulders.

name: Band Front Lateral Raise
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold the band ahead of your thighs with your palms facing down. Maintain straight arms and lift the band up in front of you until your arms are parallel to the ground. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides to about shoulder height without leaning or shrugging. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Band Front Raise
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold the band ahead of your thighs with your palms facing down. Maintain straight arms and With control raise them forward until they are parallel to the ground. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Lift the arms forward to about shoulder height, keeping the ribs down and torso still. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Band Good Morning (Pull Through)
description: Loop the band around a post. Standing a little ways away, loop the opposite end around the neck. Your hands can help hold the band in position. Begin by bending at the hips, getting your butt back as far as possible. Keep your back flat and bend forward to about 90 degrees. Your knees should be only slightly bent. Return to the starting position be driving through with the hips to come back to a standing position.

name: Band Hip Adductions
description: Anchor a band around a solid post or other object. Stand with your left side to the post, and put your right foot through the band, getting it around the ankle. Stand up straight and hold onto the post if needed. This will be your starting position. Keeping the knee straight, raise your right legs out to the side as far as you can. Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired rep count. Switch sides.

name: Band Hip Lift
description: After choosing a suitable band, lay down in the middle of the rack, after securing the band on either side of you. If your rack doesn't have pegs, the band can be secured using heavy dumbbells or similar objects, just ensure they won't move. Adjust your position so that the band is directly over your hips. Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor. Your hands can be on the floor or holding the band in position. Keeping your shoulders on the ground, drive through your heels to raise your hips, pushing into the band as high as you can. Pause at the top of the motion, and return to the starting position.

name: Band Hip Thrusts On Knees
description: Begin by kneeling on the ground with your knees about hip width and your feet flexed. Loop the resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Plant the feet and keep the ribs from flaring as the hips prepare to rise. Press through the feet and lift your hips until your torso and thighs line up. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the hips steadily and keep the feet planted for the next lift.

name: Band Jack Knife Sit-Up
description: Settle onto your back with your legs straight and your arms extended overhead, holding the band. Tighten your midsection and lift your legs and upper body simultaneously, bringing your hands toward your feet. Set the pelvis and keep the neck relaxed before curling upward. Curl your rib cage toward your pelvis, letting the abdominals move the torso. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the shoulders or torso with control before the next curl.

name: Band Kneeling Single-Arm Pulldown
description: Connect the band to a sturdy anchor point above your head. Kneel and hold the band with one hand, palm facing down. Sit tall and set the shoulders before drawing the handle down. Pull the handle down by driving your elbows toward your ribs; keep your torso steady. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Let the handle rise steadily until the arms are long, then reset the shoulders; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Band Kneeling Twisting Crunch
description: Connect the band to a sturdy anchor point at waist height. Kneel turned away from the anchor point and hold the band with both hands, keeping your elbows bent and close to your sides. Set the pelvis and keep the neck relaxed before curling upward. Curl your rib cage toward your pelvis, letting the abdominals move the torso. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the shoulders or torso with control before the next curl.

name: Band Leg Extension
description: Connect the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point and secure it around your ankle. Face the anchor point from a stable stance with feet about shoulder width. Set the pad just above the ankles and keep the thighs against the seat. Straighten your knees to lift the pad, keeping your hips against the seat. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Return along the same path at a controlled pace.

name: Band Lying Hip Internal Rotation
description: Settle onto your back with your legs straight and a resistance band looped around your feet. Bend your knees and bring them toward your chest, keeping your feet together. Set the pelvis and make the turn through the rib cage. Turn through the torso while the hips and lower body stay as steady as the setup allows. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Return through center before turning to the other side.

name: Band Lying Straight-Leg Raise
description: Settle onto your back with your legs straight and your feet together. Set the band around the arches of your feet and hold the ends of the band with your hands. Brace the abdomen and keep the shoulders anchored to the support. Lift your legs by bracing your trunk and moving at the hips rather than swinging. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the legs slowly without swinging or losing your trunk position.

name: Band Pull Through
description: Connect a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at ground level. Face the away from the anchor point from a stable stance with feet about shoulder width. Unlock the knees and brace the abdomen before moving the hips back. Push the hips back while keeping the load close and the spine steady. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Drive the hips forward to stand tall without leaning back at the top.

name: Band Pull-Apart with External Rotation
description: Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart, chest out, and shoulders back. Hold the resistance band with both hands, palms facing up or facing each other, depending on the band type. Bend your elbows at a 90-degree angle and glue your upper arms to your sides. The band should have some tension in the starting position, with your hands closer together in front of your stomach. Rotate Outward: While keeping your elbows tucked into your sides, slowly move your hands away from each other, stretching the band. Squeeze: Squeeze your shoulder blades together and down as you rotate your hands outward. Range of Motion: Rotate your hands as far outward as you comfortably can without allowing your elbows to leave your sides. Hold: Hold the end position for 1–2 seconds to maximize muscle engagement. Return: Slowly and with control, bring your hands back to the starting position.

name: Band Push Sit-Up
description: Connect the band securely to a stable anchor point. Settle onto your back with your knees bent and feet planted. Set the pelvis and keep the neck relaxed before curling upward. Curl your rib cage toward your pelvis, letting the abdominals move the torso. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the shoulders or torso with control before the next curl.

name: Band Reverse Fly
description: Connect the band to a stationary object at chest height. Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold the band with both hands in front of you. Keep a soft elbow bend and set the shoulders before moving the arms. Open your arms out and back with a slight elbow bend, drawing the shoulder blades together. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Open the arms back along the same arc without dropping the load.

name: Band Reverse Wrist Curl
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your feet planted. Take hold of the band with palms facing down, and wrap it around your fingers. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands.

name: Band Seated Biceps Curl
description: Take a seat on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take hold of the resistance band with palms facing up, and arms extended down by your sides. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Band Seated Chest Press
description: Take a seat on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take hold of the resistance band handles in each hand, with your palms facing down and elbows bent at a 90-degree angle. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Band Seated Hip Abduction
description: Take a seat on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet planted. Loop the resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Square the pelvis before moving the working leg. Open the knees or legs against resistance without shifting your torso. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Return along the same path at a controlled pace.

name: Band Seated Hip Internal Rotation
description: Take a seat on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet planted. Set a resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Set the pelvis and make the turn through the rib cage. Turn through the torso while the hips and lower body stay as steady as the setup allows. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Return through center before turning to the other side.

name: Band Seated Shoulder Press
description: Take a seat on a chair or bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take hold of the resistance band with both hands, palms facing forward, and bring it up to shoulder level. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Band Seated Straight Back Row
description: Take a seat on the floor with your legs extended and loop the resistance band around your feet. Take hold of the ends of the resistance band with your hands, palms facing each other. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch.

name: Band Seated Twist
description: Take a seat on the ground with your legs extended in front of you and your back straight. Loop the band around your waist and hold the ends with both hands. Set the pelvis and make the turn through the rib cage. Turn through the torso while the hips and lower body stay as steady as the setup allows. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Return through center before turning to the other side.

name: Band Shoulder Press
description: To begin, stand on an exercise band so that tension begins at arm's length. Grasp the handles and lift them so that the hands are at shoulder height at each side. Rotate the wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing forward. Your elbows should be bent, with the upper arms and forearms in line to the torso. This is your starting position. As you exhale, lift the handles up until your arms are fully extended overhead.

name: Band Shrug
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and place the band under your feet, holding the ends with your hands. Maintain straight arms and relaxed, and let the band hang ahead of your thighs. Let the arms hang long and keep the head neutral. Lift your shoulders toward your ears without bending the elbows or rolling the shoulders. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Return along the same path at a controlled pace.

name: Band Side Triceps Extension
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold the band with both hands, palms facing down. Reach your arms straight out to the sides, keeping them parallel to the ground. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep.

name: Band Single Leg Calf Raise
description: Stand and set your feet about hip width and place the band around the ball of your left foot. Use a stable object for balance if needed. Let the ankles move freely while the rest of the body stays quiet. Rise through the balls of your feet, lifting the heels as high as you can without rocking. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the heels at a measured pace before rising again.

name: Band Single Leg Reverse Calf Raise
description: Stand and set your feet about hip width and place the band around the ball of your foot. Use a stable object for balance. Let the ankles move freely while the rest of the body stays quiet. Rise through the balls of your feet, lifting the heels as high as you can without rocking. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the heels at a measured pace before rising again.

name: Band Single Leg Split Squat
description: Stand and set your feet about hip width and place a resistance band around your ankles. Step wide forward with your right foot and a smaller step back with your left foot. Brace the abdomen and spread pressure across the whole foot. Bend at the hips and knees to lower, keeping your feet grounded and knees tracking with the toes. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Stand fully, reset your footing and breathing, then begin the next descent.

name: Band Single-Arm Overhead Biceps Curl
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and place one end of the band under your foot. Take hold of the other end of the band with your arm straight overhead, palm facing forward. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Band Single-Arm Single Leg Split Squat
description: Stand and set your feet about hip width and place a resistance band around your ankles. Reach one leg forward and rest the top of your foot on a bench or step behind you. Brace the abdomen and spread pressure across the whole foot. Bend at the hips and knees to lower, keeping your feet grounded and knees tracking with the toes. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Stand fully, reset your footing and breathing, then begin the next descent; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Band Single-Arm Standing Low Row
description: Connect the band to a stable anchor point at waist height. Face the anchor point from a stable stance with feet about shoulder width. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Band Single-Arm Twisting Chest Press
description: Connect the band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Stand and set your side facing the anchor point and grab the band with one hand. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weights up while turning the palms inward; reverse the turn as you lower. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Band Single-Arm Twisting Seated Row
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your feet planted and your back straight. Take hold of the band with one hand and extend your arm fully in front of you. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Band Skull Crusher
description: Secure a band to the base of a rack or the bench. Lay on the bench so that the band is lined up with your head. Take hold of the band, raising your elbows so that the upper arm is perpendicular to the floor. With the elbow flexed, the band should be above your head. This will be your starting position. Extend through the elbow to straighten your arm, keeping your upper arm in place. Pause at the top of the motion, and return to the starting position.

name: Band Squat
description: Set up the bands on the sleeves, secured to either band pegs, the rack, or dumbbells so that there is appropriate tension. Begin by stepping under the bar and placing it across the back of the shoulders. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and rotate your elbows forward, attempting to bend the bar across your shoulders. Remove the bar from the rack, creating a tight arch in your lower back, and step back into position. Place your feet wide for more emphasis on the back, glutes, adductors, and hamstrings. Keep your head facing forward. With your back, shoulders, and core tight, push your knees and butt out and you begin your descent. Sit back with your hips as much as possible. Ideally, your shins should be perpendicular to the ground. Lower bar position necessitates a greater torso lean to keep the bar over the heels. Continue until you break parallel, which is defined as the crease of the hip being in line with the top of the knee. Keeping the weight on your heels and pushing your feet and knees out, drive upward as you lead the movement with your head. Continue upward, maintaining tightness head to toe, until you have returned to the starting position.

name: Band Squat Row
description: Connect the band to a sturdy anchor point at waist height. Face the anchor point from a stable stance with feet about shoulder width. Brace the abdomen and spread pressure across the whole foot. Bend at the hips and knees to lower, keeping your feet grounded and knees tracking with the toes. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Stand fully, reset your footing and breathing, then begin the next descent.

name: Band Standing Crunch
description: Connect the band to a sturdy anchor point at waist height. Face the away from the anchor point from a stable stance with feet about shoulder width. Set the pelvis and keep the neck relaxed before curling upward. Curl your rib cage toward your pelvis, letting the abdominals move the torso. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the shoulders or torso with control before the next curl.

name: Band Standing Rear Delt Row
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and place the band under your feet. Take hold of the band handles with your palms facing each other and your arms extended in front of you. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch.

name: Band Standing Twisting Crunch
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and place the band around your upper back, crossing it ahead of your chest. Take hold of the ends of the band with your hands, keeping your elbows bent and close to your sides. Set the pelvis and keep the neck relaxed before curling upward. Curl your rib cage toward your pelvis, letting the abdominals move the torso. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the shoulders or torso with control before the next curl.

name: Band Step-Up
description: Set a band around your thighs, just above your knees. Face a step or platform with your feet about hip width. Put the lead foot fully on the platform before shifting your weight onto it. Step onto the platform and drive through the lead foot to stand tall on it. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Push through the lead foot to return to the start, then change legs as planned.

name: Band Stiff Leg Deadlift
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and place the band around your ankles. Take hold of the band with both hands ahead of your thighs, palms facing your body. Unlock the knees and brace the abdomen before moving the hips back. Push the hips back while keeping the load close and the spine steady. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Drive the hips forward to stand tall without leaning back at the top.

name: Band Straight Back Stiff Leg Deadlift
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and place the band around your upper legs. Take hold of the band with both hands ahead of your thighs, palms facing your body. Unlock the knees and brace the abdomen before moving the hips back. Push the hips back while keeping the load close and the spine steady. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Drive the hips forward to stand tall without leaning back at the top.

name: Band Straight-Leg Deadlift
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and place the band around your feet. Take hold of the band with both hands, palms facing your body, and keep your arms straight. Unlock the knees and brace the abdomen before moving the hips back. Send your hips back with a soft knee bend, lowering the load close to your legs until the hamstrings stretch. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Drive the hips forward to stand tall without leaning back at the top.

name: Band Terminal Knee Extension
description: This is an end range strengthening exercise for the knee extensors. Start by looping a band around the back of one knee and anchoring the other end to a stable surface in front of you. Stand in a split stance with the banded knee bent and placed as the front leg. Straighten the knee to pull against the bands resistance and maintain a contraction in your quadriceps for up to 5 seconds before releasing.

name: Band Twisting Overhead Press
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and place the band under your feet. Take hold of the band handles at shoulder height with your palms facing forward. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weights up while turning the palms inward; reverse the turn as you lower. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Band Two-Leg Calf Raise - (Band Under Both Legs)
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and place a resistance band under both feet. Take hold of the ends of the band with your hands for stability. Let the ankles move freely while the rest of the body stays quiet. Rise through the balls of your feet, lifting the heels as high as you can without rocking. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the heels at a measured pace before rising again.

name: Band Underhand Pulldown
description: Connect the band to a high anchor point, such as a pull-up bar or sturdy beam. Face the anchor point from a stable stance with feet about shoulder width. Sit tall and set the shoulders before drawing the handle down. Pull the handle down by driving your elbows toward your ribs; keep your torso steady. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Let the handle rise steadily until the arms are long, then reset the shoulders.

name: Band Vertical Pallof Press
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and wrap the band around a sturdy object at chest height. Take hold of the band with both hands and step away from the anchor point, creating tension in the band. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Band Wrist Curl
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your feet planted. Take hold of the band with both hands, palms facing up, and rest your forearms on your thighs. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands.

name: Band Y-Raise
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold the band ahead of your thighs with your palms facing inwards. Maintain straight arms and lift them up and out to the sides, forming a 'Y' shape with your body. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Raise the arms diagonally into a Y shape while keeping the shoulders away from your ears. Control the band on the way back instead of letting it snap you into position. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Banded Ankle Mobility
description: Anchor a resistance band low behind you, for example at the bottom of a rack, and loop it around the front of your ankle, just above the foot. Get into a half-kneeling position with the banded foot in front, so that the band pulls your ankle backwards. Keeping your heel on the floor, drive your knee forward over your toes, then return under control. Repeat for several reps and switch sides.

name: Banded Clamshell
description: Position Side plank with the elbow and the forearm on the ground and the legs slightly bent. Stretch a doubled-up resistance band between your thighs, just above the knee. Execution Lift your upper knee while keeping your feet close together, like a “shell opening,” then slowly return to the starting position. Keep your core stable and your hips aligned.

name: Banded Front Raise
description: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet about hip-width apart, holding one end in each hand in front of your thighs. Keeping your arms straight with a slight bend in the elbows, raise your hands forward to shoulder height, then lower slowly under control. Can be done with both arms together or alternating. Use a heavier band or shorten the band to increase resistance.

name: Banded Monster Walk
description: A banded walking drill for the glutes and hip stabilisers. Place a mini band around both thighs just above the knees, or around the ankles for a harder version. Stand with feet hip-width apart so the band is under tension, then sink into a quarter-squat with the chest up. Walk forward with small diagonal steps, pushing each leg out against the band and keeping the knees tracking over the toes rather than letting them fall inward. Walk forward for the prescribed number of steps, then walk backward to return, keeping the band under tension throughout.

name: Banded Scapular Retraction
description: Attach one end of resistance band to wall/upright/... at shoulder height. Insert arm into the loop, at the tricep. Step back until band is pulled straight. Pull back elbow and shoulder against the resistance of the band.

name: Banded Shoulder Drills
description: Attach a resistance band to something solid behind you. Stand away from it, holding it in your hand so it is taut. Perform the shoulder mobility and rotation drills shown in the video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zdwEWchSjrI

name: Barbell Ab Rollout - On Knees
description: Hold an Olympic barbell loaded with 5-10lbs on each side and kneel on the floor. Now place the barbell on the floor in front of you so that you are on all your hands and knees (as in a kneeling push up position). This will be your starting position. Slowly roll the barbell straight forward, stretching your body into a straight position. Tip: Go down as far as you can without touching the floor with your body. Breathe in during this portion of the movement. After a second pause at the stretched position, start pulling yourself back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Go slowly and keep your abs tight at all times.

name: Barbell Alternate Biceps Curl
description: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder width and hold a barbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
