Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Dumbbell Kickbacks on Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and your back straight. Take a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Hold the upper arm beside your torso and straighten the elbow behind you. Keep the ball steady and use the feet to manage your balance. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Kneeling Biceps Curl Exercise Ball
description: Get down on the floor with an exercise ball in front of you. Set your elbows on top of the exercise ball, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing up. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep the ball steady and use the feet to manage your balance. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Lateral to Front Raise
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body. Keep your spine in a comfortable neutral position and Brace your trunk. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Lift the arms forward to about shoulder height, keeping the ribs down and torso still. Stop near shoulder height rather than shrugging to lift higher. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Dumbbell Lunge
description: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. This will be your starting position. Step forward with your right leg around 2 feet or so from the foot being left stationary behind and lower your upper body down, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Note: As in the other exercises, do not allow your knee to go forward beyond your toes as you come down, as this will put undue stress on the knee joint. Make sure that you keep your front shin perpendicular to the ground. Using mainly the heel of your foot, push up and go back to the starting position as you exhale. Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.

name: Dumbbell Lunge With Biceps Curl
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward. Step forward with your right foot, lowering your body into a lunge position. Your right knee should be bent at a 90-degree angle and your left knee should be hovering just above the ground. Set your stance wide enough to balance before bending either knee. Step into the movement and bend both knees, keeping your front foot planted. Keep the front foot planted and avoid collapsing inward at the knee. Push through the lead foot to return to the start, then change legs as planned.

name: Dumbbell Lying Alternate Extension
description: Settle onto a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Reach your arms straight up over your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Lying Elbow Press
description: Settle onto a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other and arms extended straight up over your chest. Lower the dumbbells toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, With the upper arms still. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep the wrists stacked and use a shoulder path that feels natural. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Dumbbell Lying Extension (across Face)
description: Settle onto a bench with your feet planted and your head at the end of the bench. Take a dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up above your chest, palms facing each other. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Keep the upper arms steady while the forearms travel. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation
description: Settle onto your side on a flat bench with your upper arm against your side and your elbow bent 90 degrees. Take a dumbbell in your hand with your palm facing down. Set the pelvis and make the turn through the rib cage. Turn through the torso while the hips and lower body stay as steady as the setup allows. Keep the turn smooth instead of throwing the arms across the body. Return through center before turning to the other side.

name: Dumbbell Lying Hammer Press
description: Settle onto a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other and arms extended straight up. Before moving, lower the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep the palms facing each other and the wrists straight. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Dumbbell Lying on Floor Rear Delt Raise
description: Position yourself face down on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Reach your arms straight out in front of you, keeping a slight bend in your elbows. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Lift the arms out and back with soft elbows, letting the rear shoulders do the work. Stop near shoulder height rather than shrugging to lift higher. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Dumbbell Lying One-Arm Rear Lateral Raise
description: While holding a dumbbell in one hand, lay with your chest down on a slightly inclined (around 15 degrees when measured from the floor) adjustable bench. The other hand can be used to hold to the leg of the bench for stability. Position the palm of the hand that is holding the dumbbell in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arm extended with the elbow slightly bent. This will be your starting position. Now raise the arm with the dumbbell to the side until your elbow is at shoulder height and your arm is roughly parallel to the floor as you exhale. Tip: Maintain your arm perpendicular to the torso while keeping your arm extended throughout the movement. Also, keep the contraction at the top for a second. Slowly lower the dumbbell to the starting position as you inhale. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation
description: Lie on a flat bench face down with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it. Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm. Now raise the upper arm so that the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the upper arm is perpendicular to your torso. Tip: The upper arm should be parallel to the floor and also creating a 90-degree angle with your torso. This will be your starting position. As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted forward as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is parallel to the floor. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second. As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation on Floor
description: Settle onto the floor with your face down and your arms extended straight out in front of you, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Rotate your palms so they are facing down toward the floor. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Use a small, smooth range without swinging the elbows. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands.

name: Dumbbell Lying Pullover on Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball and roll forward until your upper back is resting on the ball. Take a dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up over your chest. Set the ribs down and keep a small elbow bend before lowering the weight. Lower the weight in an arc behind your head until you feel a comfortable shoulder stretch. Keep the ball steady and use the feet to manage your balance. Pull the weight back over the chest along the same arc, without lifting the ribs.

name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Delt Row
description: Position yourself face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards. Extend your arms straight down toward the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Bring the elbows back without jerking the torso. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch.

name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise
description: While holding a dumbbell in each hand, lay with your chest down on a slightly inclined (around 15 degrees when measured from the floor) adjustable bench. Position the palms of the hands in a neutral manner (palms facing your torso) as you keep the arms extended with the elbows slightly bent. This will be your starting position. Now raise the arms to the side until your elbows are at shoulder height and your arms are roughly parallel to the floor as you exhale. Tip: Maintain your arms perpendicular to the torso while keeping them extended throughout the movement. Also, keep the contraction at the top for a second. Slowly lower the dumbbells to the starting position as you inhale. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.

name: Dumbbell Lying Single Extension
description: Settle onto a bench with a dumbbell in one hand and your arm straight above your chest. Lower the dumbbell in a controlled manner toward your forehead, keeping your upper arm stationary. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Keep the upper arms steady while the forearms travel. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Lying Single-Arm Deltoid Rear
description: Position yourself face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing inwards. Extend your arm straight down toward the floor, keeping it close to your body. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Lift the weights away from your torso to about shoulder height, keeping the elbows softly bent. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Lying Single-Arm Press
description: Settle onto a bench with your back supported and feet planted. Take a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing toward your feet. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Lying Single-Arm Pronated Triceps Extension
description: Settle onto a bench with your back and head supported, and your feet planted. Take a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing down, and extend your arm straight up above your shoulder. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Lying Single-Arm Rear Lateral Raise
description: Position yourself face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, hanging toward the floor. Keep the arm straight and lift the dumbbell out to the side, away from your body. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides to about shoulder height without leaning or shrugging. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Lying Single-Arm Supinated Triceps Extension
description: Settle onto a bench with your back and head supported, and your feet planted. Take a dumbbell in one hand with palms facing up, and extend your arm straight up above your shoulder. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Lying Supination
description: Lie sideways on a flat bench with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it. Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm. Now raise the upper arm so that the forearm is parallel to the floor and perpendicular to your torso (Tip: So the forearm will be directly in front of you). The upper arm will be stationary by your torso and should be parallel to the floor (aligned with your torso at all times). This will be your starting position. As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted up in a semicircle motion as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the torso pointing towards the ceiling. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second. As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then switch to the other arm.

name: Dumbbell Lying Supination on Floor
description: Settle onto your back on the floor with your legs extended and your arms by your sides, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Before moving, rotate your palms to face up, keeping your elbows close to your sides. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Use a small, smooth range without swinging the elbows. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands.

name: Dumbbell Lying Supine Biceps Curl
description: Settle onto a bench with your back and head supported, and your feet planted. Take a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing up and your arms straight. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep the torso quiet and let the elbow bend lift the weight. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Lying Supine Curl
description: Lie down on a flat bench face up while holding a dumbbell in each arm on top of your thighs. Bring the dumbbells to the sides with the arms extended and the palms of the hands facing your thighs (neutral grip). While keeping the arms close to your torso and elbows in, slowly lower your arms (as you keep them extended with a slight bend at the elbows) as far down towards the floor as you can go. Once you cannot go down any further, lock your upper arms in that position and that will be your starting position. As you breathe out, slowly begin to curl the weights up as you simultaneously rotate your wrists so that the palms of the hands face up. Continue curling the weight until your biceps are fully contracted and squeeze hard at the top position for a second. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Upper arms should remain stationary and elbows should stay in throughout the movement. Return back to the starting position very slowly.

name: Dumbbell Lying Wide Curl
description: Settle onto a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up and arms straight. With your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep the torso quiet and let the elbow bend lift the weight. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Neutral Grip Bench Press
description: Take a dumbbell in each hand and lay back onto a flat bench. Your feet should be flat on the floor and your shoulder blades retracted. Maintaining a neutral grip, palms facing each other, begin with your arms extended directly above you, perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position. Begin the movement by flexing the elbow, lowering the upper arms to the side. Descend until the dumbbells are to your torso. Pause, then extend the elbow and return to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell One-Arm Triceps Extension
description: Grab a dumbbell and either sit on a military press bench or a utility bench that has a back support on it as you place the dumbbells upright on top of your thighs or stand up straight. Clean the dumbbell up to bring it to shoulder height and then extend the arm over your head so that the whole arm is perpendicular to the floor and next to your head. The dumbbell should be on top of you. The other hand can be kept fully extended to the side, by the waist, supporting the upper arm that has the dumbbell or grabbing a fixed surface. Rotate the wrist so that the palm of your hand is facing forward and the pinkie is facing the ceiling. This will be your starting position. Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head as you hold the upper arm stationary. Inhale as you perform this movement and pause when your triceps are fully stretched. Return to the starting position by flexing your triceps as you breathe out. Tip: It is imperative that only the forearm moves. The upper arm should remain at all times stationary next to your head. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One-Arm Upright Row
description: Grab a dumbbell and stand up straight with your arm extended in front of you with a slight bend at the elbows and your back straight. This will be your starting position. Tip: The dumbbell should be resting on top of your thigh with the palm of your hands facing your thighs. Keep the other hand can be kept fully extended to the side, by the waist or grabbing a fixed surface. This will be your starting position. Use your side shoulders to lift the dumbbell as you exhale. The dumbbell should be close to the body as you move it up. Continue to lift it until the dumbbell is nearly in line with your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the dumbbell, your elbow should always be higher than your forearm. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement. Lower the dumbbell back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench Neutral Wrist Curl
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up. Support the forearms on the bench while leaving the wrists free beyond its edge. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Use a small, smooth range without swinging the elbows. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench Reverse Wrist Curl
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing down. Support the forearms on the bench while leaving the wrists free beyond its edge. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Use a small, smooth range without swinging the elbows. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench Single-Arm Neutral Wrist Curl
description: Take a seat on a bench with a dumbbell in one hand and your arm extended over the bench, palm facing up. Keep your upper arm stationary and curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder, keeping your wrist in a neutral position. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench Single-Arm Reverse Wrist Curl
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down. Set your forearm on the bench with your wrist hanging off the edge. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench Single-Arm Wrist Curl
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down. Set your forearm on the bench with your wrist hanging off the edge. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench Wrist Curl
description: Take a seat on a bench with your forearms resting on the bench and your palms facing up, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Let your wrists to hang over the edge of the bench. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Use a small, smooth range without swinging the elbows. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands.

name: Dumbbell Palm Rotational Bent Over Row
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing down. Bend forward at the hips, with your spine steady and your knees soft. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Bring the elbows back without jerking the torso. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch.

name: Dumbbell Palms in Incline Bench Press
description: Angle the bench to roughly 45 degrees. Take a seat on the bench with your back against the backrest and feet planted. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep the wrists stacked and use a shoulder path that feels natural. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Dumbbell Plyo Squat
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Before moving, lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back. Brace the abdomen and spread pressure across the whole foot. Bend at the hips and knees to lower, keeping your feet grounded and knees tracking with the toes. Drive upward with the chest and hips rising together; keep the knees from collapsing inward. Stand fully, reset your footing and breathing, then begin the next descent.

name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl Over Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and your back straight. Take a dumbbell in one hand with palms facing up, resting your elbow on the exercise ball. Set the working upper arm against the preacher pad and leave the elbow free to bend. Curl the weight while your upper arms stay in contact with the pad. Keep the ball steady and use the feet to manage your balance. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Preacher Hammer Curl
description: Place the upper part of both arms on top of the preacher bench as you hold a dumbbell in each hand with the palms facing each other (neutral grip). As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched. As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard for a second at the contracted position and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Press on Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and dumbbells in each hand, resting on your thighs. With control walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball until your lower back is supported on the ball and your knees are at a 90-degree angle. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep the ball steady and use the feet to manage your balance. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Dumbbell Pronate-Grip Triceps Extension
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your back straight and feet planted. Take a dumbbell with both hands, palms facing down, and extend your arms straight up overhead. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Keep the upper arms steady while the forearms travel. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
description: Grab a dumbbell on each hand and lie face down on an incline bench with your shoulders near top of the incline. Your knees can rest on the seat or your legs can be straddled to the sides (my preferred way). Let your arms extend and hang naturally in front of you so that they are perpendicular to the floor. Now keep your elbows in by your side and face the palms forward. This will be your starting position. Raise the dumbbells by contracting the biceps until your arms are fully flexed. Exhale as you perform this portion of the movement and ensure that only the forearms move. The upper arms should remain stationary at all times. Lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended. Repeat for the recommended amount of times.

name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Hammer Curl
description: Set the bench to a 45-degree incline. Position yourself face down on the bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl with palms facing each other and elbows near your sides; avoid rocking back. Keep the palms facing each other and the wrists straight. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Pullover Hip Extension on Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and the dumbbell resting on your thighs. With control walk your feet forward, rolling the exercise ball down your back until your head, neck, and upper back are supported on the ball. Set the ribs down and keep a small elbow bend before lowering the weight. Lower the weight in an arc behind your head until you feel a comfortable shoulder stretch. Keep the ball steady and use the feet to manage your balance. Pull the weight back over the chest along the same arc, without lifting the ribs.

name: Dumbbell Pullover on Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball and hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest, arms extended. With control lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your arms straight. Set the ribs down and keep a small elbow bend before lowering the weight. Lower the weight in an arc behind your head until you feel a comfortable shoulder stretch. Keep the ball steady and use the feet to manage your balance. Pull the weight back over the chest along the same arc, without lifting the ribs.

name: Dumbbell Push-Up
description: Normal Push-ups on Dumbbells, this brings a further range of movement

name: Dumbbell Raise
description: Grab a dumbbell in each arm and stand up straight with your arms extended by your sides with a slight bend at the elbows and your back straight. This will be your starting position. Tip: The dumbbell should be next to your thighs with the palm of your hands facing back. Use your side shoulders to lift the dumbbells as you exhale. The dumbbells should be to the side of the body as you move them up. Continue to lift it until the dumbbells are nearly in line with your chin. Tip: Your elbows should drive the motion. As you lift the dumbbell, your elbow should always be higher than your forearm. Also, keep your torso stationary and pause for a second at the top of the movement. Lower the dumbbells back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, with your spine steady. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Lift the arms out and back with soft elbows, letting the rear shoulders do the work. Stop near shoulder height rather than shrugging to lift higher. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
description: Hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend at your hips to make your back almost parallel to the floor. Let your arms hang down. Keep your arms in line with your shoulders. bend and lift your elbows out to the sides until your upper arms are parallel to the floor. Slowly return and repeat

name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row (shoulder)
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and knees soft. Take a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Bring the elbows back without jerking the torso. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch.

name: Dumbbell Rear Fly
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, with your spine steady. Keep a soft elbow bend and set the shoulders before moving the arms. With a soft bend in the elbows, sweep your arms together in a wide arc. Keep the elbow angle nearly unchanged through the arc. Open the arms back along the same arc without dropping the load.

name: Dumbbell Rear Lateral Raise
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, with your spine steady and core engaged. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides to about shoulder height without leaning or shrugging. Stop near shoulder height rather than shrugging to lift higher. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Dumbbell Rear Lateral Raise (support Head)
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, with your spine steady. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides to about shoulder height without leaning or shrugging. Stop near shoulder height rather than shrugging to lift higher. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Dumbbell Rear Lunge
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Step backward with your right foot, lowering your body into a lunge position. Set your stance wide enough to balance before bending either knee. Step into the movement and bend both knees, keeping your front foot planted. Keep the front foot planted and avoid collapsing inward at the knee. Push through the lead foot to return to the start, then change legs as planned.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Bench Press
description: Settle onto a bench with your feet planted and your knees bent. Take a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing down, palms facing toward your feet. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep the wrists stacked and use a shoulder path that feels natural. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Preacher Curl
description: Take a seat on a preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the pad and your chest against the support. Take a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing up. Set the working upper arm against the preacher pad and leave the elbow free to bend. Curl the weight while your upper arms stay in contact with the pad. Keep the torso quiet and let the elbow bend lift the weight. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Spider Curl
description: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body and arms straight. With your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl the weight with your palms facing down, keeping the elbows close and torso still. Keep the torso quiet and let the elbow bend lift the weight. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Reverse-Grip Biceps Curl
description: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing down and arms straight. With your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl the weight with your palms facing down, keeping the elbows close and torso still. Keep the palms in the chosen grip without bending the wrists back. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Reverse-Grip Incline Bench Single-Arm Row
description: Angle the bench to roughly 45 degrees. Set a dumbbell on the floor next to the bench. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Reverse-Grip Incline Bench Two-Arm Row
description: Angle the bench to roughly 45 degrees. Take a seat on the bench with your chest against the backrest and your feet planted. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Keep the palms in the chosen grip without bending the wrists back. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch.

name: Dumbbell Reverse-Grip Row
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and knees soft. Take a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing down, palms facing your body. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Keep the palms in the chosen grip without bending the wrists back. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch.

name: Dumbbell Rotation Reverse Fly
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, with your spine steady and chest up. Keep a soft elbow bend and set the shoulders before moving the arms. Open your arms out and back with a slight elbow bend, drawing the shoulder blades together. Keep the elbow angle nearly unchanged through the arc. Open the arms back along the same arc without dropping the load.

name: Dumbbell Scaption
description: This corrective exercise strengthens the muscles that stabilize your shoulder blade. Hold a light weight in each hand, hanging at your sides. Your thumbs should pointing up. Begin the movement raising your arms out in front of you, about 30 degrees off center. Your arms should be fully extended as you perform the movement. Continue until your arms are parallel to the ground, and then return to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Scott Press
description: Take a seat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward. Before moving, raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, with your elbows bent and palms facing forward. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep the wrists stacked and use a shoulder path that feels natural. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Front Raise
description: Take a seat on a bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body and arms extended down by your sides. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Lift the arms forward to about shoulder height, keeping the ribs down and torso still. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Hammer Curl on Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and your back straight. Take a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body and your arms straight. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl with palms facing each other and elbows near your sides; avoid rocking back. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Press
description: Take a seat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward. Before moving, raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, with your elbows bent and palms facing forward. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bench Extension
description: Take a seat on a bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take a dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight up above your head. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Keep the upper arms steady while the forearms travel. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bent Arm Lateral Raise
description: Take a seat on a bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides to about shoulder height without leaning or shrugging. Stop near shoulder height rather than shrugging to lift higher. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bent Over Alternate Kickback
description: Take a seat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards. Bend forward at the waist, with your spine steady and parallel to the ground. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Hold the upper arm beside your torso and straighten the elbow behind you. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bent Over Triceps Extension
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend forward at the waist, with your spine steady and your head up. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Keep the upper arms steady while the forearms travel. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Seated Biceps Curl
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up. Keep your spine in a comfortable neutral position and your elbows close to your torso. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep the torso quiet and let the elbow bend lift the weight. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Seated Biceps Curl (on Stability Ball)
description: Take a seat on a stability ball with your feet planted and your back straight. Take a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward and your arms straight. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep the ball steady and use the feet to manage your balance. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Seated Biceps Curl to Shoulder Press
description: Take a seat on a bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward and arms straight. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep the torso quiet and let the elbow bend lift the weight. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Seated Box Jump
description: Position a box a couple feet to the side of a bench. Hold a dumbbell to your chest with both hands and seat yourself on the bench facing the box. This will be your starting position. Plant your feet firmly on the ground as you lean forward, extending through the hips and knees to jump up and forward. Land on the box with both feet, absorbing the impact by allowing the hips and knees to bend. Step down and return to the starting position.

name: Dumbbell Seated Calf Raise
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your feet planted and a dumbbell resting on your thighs. Set the balls of your feet on a raised surface such as a step or block, with your heels hanging off the edge. Let the ankles move freely while the rest of the body stays quiet. Rise through the balls of your feet, lifting the heels as high as you can without rocking. Pause at the top without rolling the ankles outward. Lower the heels at a measured pace before rising again.

name: Dumbbell Seated Front Raise
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs. Keep your spine in a comfortable neutral position and core engaged. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Lift the arms forward to about shoulder height, keeping the ribs down and torso still. Stop near shoulder height rather than shrugging to lift higher. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Dumbbell Seated Hammer Curl
description: Take a seat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso and arms extended straight down. With your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the weights while contracting your biceps. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl with palms facing each other and elbows near your sides; avoid rocking back. Keep the palms facing each other and the wrists straight. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Seated Inner Biceps Curl
description: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso. Rotate the palms of the hands so that they are facing inward in a neutral position. This will be your starting position. While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the dumbbells out and up, turning the palms out as you lift and keeping your forearms in line with your outer deltoids. Tips: Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position as your breathe in. Remember to rotate your arms as you lower the dumbbells so that you can switch back to a neutral grip. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Seated Kickback
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees slightly and lean forward from your hips, with your spine steady. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Hold the upper arm beside your torso and straighten the elbow behind you. Keep the upper arms steady while the forearms travel. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Seated Lateral Raise
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; a dumbbell in each hand, resting on your thighs. Keep your spine in a comfortable neutral position and core engaged. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides to about shoulder height without leaning or shrugging. Stop near shoulder height rather than shrugging to lift higher. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Dumbbell Seated Neutral Wrist Curl
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Set your forearms on your thighs, letting the dumbbells to hang down. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Use a small, smooth range without swinging the elbows. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands.

name: Dumbbell Seated Palms Up Wrist Curl
description: Start out by placing two dumbbells on the floor in front of a flat bench. Sit down on the edge of the flat bench with your legs at about shoulder width apart. Make sure to keep your feet on the floor. Use your arms to grab both of the dumbbells and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against your thighs with the palms of the hands facing up. Your wrists should be hanging over the edge of your thighs. Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling. Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling. Make sure to inhale during this part of the exercise. Tip: Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement needed to perform this exercise. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions. When finished, simply lower the dumbbells to the floor.

name: Dumbbell Seated Preacher Curl
description: Take a seat on a preacher curl bench with your feet planted. Take a dumbbell in one hand with palms facing up, resting your upper arm against the preacher pad. Set the working upper arm against the preacher pad and leave the elbow free to bend. Curl the weight while your upper arms stay in contact with the pad. Keep the torso quiet and let the elbow bend lift the weight. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Seated Reverse-Grip Concentration Curl
description: Sit with both feet grounded and hold one dumbbell with the palm facing down. Set your elbow on the inside of your thigh, just above the knee. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl the dumbbell with the palm facing down while the upper arm stays braced against the inner thigh. Keep the palms in the chosen grip without bending the wrists back. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still.

name: Dumbbell Seated Reverse-Grip Single-Arm Overhead Triceps Extension
description: Take a seat on a bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take a dumbbell with palms facing up and extend your arm straight up overhead. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms pointed upward and extend at the elbows without flaring the ribs. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Seated Shoulder Press (parallel Grip)
description: Take a seat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inward. Before moving, raise the dumbbells to shoulder height, elbows bent and palms facing forward. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep the wrists stacked and use a shoulder path that feels natural. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again.

name: Dumbbell Seated Single-Arm Biceps Curl On Exercise Ball With Leg Raised
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and your back straight. Take a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your arm straight. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Seated Single-Arm Kickback
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; hold a dumbbell in one hand. Bend your torso forward at the waist, with your spine steady and parallel to the ground. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Hold the upper arm beside your torso and straighten the elbow behind you. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Seated Single-Arm Rotate
description: Take a seat on a bench with your back straight and hold a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on your thigh. Before moving, raise the dumbbell up to shoulder height, keeping your elbow close to your body. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Seated Single-Leg Calf Raise
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your feet planted and a dumbbell resting on your right thigh. Reach your left leg straight out in front of you, keeping your foot flexed. Let the ankles move freely while the rest of the body stays quiet. Rise through the balls of your feet, lifting the heels as high as you can without rocking. Keep the pelvis level as the supporting leg does the work. Lower the heels at a measured pace before rising again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Seated Single-Leg Calf Raise - Hammer Grip
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your feet planted and a dumbbell resting on your thighs. Set one foot on a raised surface, such as a step or block, with your heel hanging off the edge. Let the ankles move freely while the rest of the body stays quiet. Rise through the balls of your feet, lifting the heels as high as you can without rocking. Keep the pelvis level as the supporting leg does the work. Lower the heels at a measured pace before rising again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Seated Single-Leg Calf Raise - Palm Up
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your back straight and your feet planted. Take a dumbbell in one hand and place it on top of your thigh, palm facing up. Let the ankles move freely while the rest of the body stays quiet. Rise through the balls of your feet, lifting the heels as high as you can without rocking. Keep the pelvis level as the supporting leg does the work. Lower the heels at a measured pace before rising again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Rotations
description: Dumbbell shoulder rotations are designed to strengthen the rotator cuff muscles and improve shoulder stability and mobility. External Rotation: Hold a dumbbell in one hand, keeping your elbow bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate your forearm outward, away from your body, keeping your elbow stationary. Slowly return to the starting position. Internal Rotation: Hold a dumbbell in one hand, keeping your elbow bent at 90 degrees and close to your body. Rotate your forearm inward, toward your body, and slowly return to the starting position. Perform the exercise with controlled movements to avoid strain.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
description: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on the left hand (palms facing the torso) as you have the right hand holding your waist. Your feet should be placed at shoulder width. This will be your starting position. While keeping your back straight and your head up, bend only at the waist to the right as far as possible. Breathe in as you bend to the side. Then hold for a second and come back up to the starting position as you exhale. Tip: Keep the rest of the body stationary. Now repeat the movement but bending to the left instead. Hold for a second and come back to the starting position. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and then change hands.

name: Dumbbell Side Plank with Rear Fly
description: Begin by lying on your side with your legs extended and stacked on top of each other. Set your forearm on the ground directly below your shoulder, keeping your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle. Brace the abdomen and find a position you can maintain without holding your breath. Brace your midsection and hold the position while breathing normally. Keep breathing steadily as you maintain the same body line. Keep the shape for the planned time, then come out of it with control.

name: Dumbbell Side Squat
description: This exercise involves holding a dumbbell in one hand and performing a squat while stepping to the side. It targets the legs, glutes, and core muscles.

name: Dumbbell Side-Lying One Hand Raise
description: Settle onto your side with your legs extended and your head supported by your arm. Take a dumbbell in your top hand with your palm facing down. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Lift the weights away from your torso to about shoulder height, keeping the elbows softly bent. Stop near shoulder height rather than shrugging to lift higher. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight.

name: Dumbbell Single Arm Overhead Carry
description: Stand tall and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in one hand. Before moving, raise the dumbbell overhead, fully extending your arm. Stand tall with the load secure and the shoulders level. Walk at a controlled pace, keeping your shoulders level and your steps even. Keep steps even and avoid leaning away from the load. Stop before posture breaks down, set the load down safely, and reset for the next walk.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Deadlift with Stepbox Support
description: Stand and set your feet about hip width, holding a dumbbell in your right hand. Set your left foot on a stepbox or elevated surface behind you. Unlock the knees and brace the abdomen before moving the hips back. Push the hips back while keeping the load close and the spine steady. Keep the weight close to the legs and stop when the back would begin to round. Drive the hips forward to stand tall without leaning back at the top.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Split Squat
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Step forward with one foot and position your feet so that your front foot is flat on the ground and your back foot is elevated on a bench or step. Brace the abdomen and spread pressure across the whole foot. Bend at the hips and knees to lower, keeping your feet grounded and knees tracking with the toes. Drive upward with the chest and hips rising together; keep the knees from collapsing inward. Stand fully, reset your footing and breathing, then begin the next descent.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Squat
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Reach one leg forward and keep it off the ground throughout the exercise. Brace the abdomen and spread pressure across the whole foot. Bend at the hips and knees to lower, keeping your feet grounded and knees tracking with the toes. Drive upward with the chest and hips rising together; keep the knees from collapsing inward. Stand fully, reset your footing and breathing, then begin the next descent.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Bench Fly
description: Take a seat on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting it on top of your thigh. Recline on the bench, keeping the dumbbell pressed against your thigh. Keep a soft elbow bend and set the shoulders before moving the arms. With a soft bend in the elbows, sweep your arms together in a wide arc. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Open the arms back along the same arc without dropping the load; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Concentration Curl (On Stability Ball)
description: Take a seat on a stability ball with your feet planted and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle. Take a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your arm extended down toward the floor. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Decline Chest Press
description: Settle onto a decline bench with a dumbbell in one hand, resting on your chest. Set your feet planted and keep your back pressed against the bench. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Fly On Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in one hand and your feet planted. Step your feet forward and roll your body down until your upper back is resting on the exercise ball. Keep a soft elbow bend and set the shoulders before moving the arms. With a soft bend in the elbows, sweep your arms together in a wide arc. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Open the arms back along the same arc without dropping the load; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm French Press On Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and your back straight. Take a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Bend the elbows to lower the bar behind your head while the upper arms stay mostly still. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Straighten the elbows to bring the bar overhead, then begin the next controlled rep; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Hammer Preacher Curl
description: Take a seat on a preacher bench with a dumbbell in one hand and your upper arm resting on the pad. Take hold of the dumbbell with a neutral grip (palms facing your body). Set the working upper arm against the preacher pad and leave the elbow free to bend. Curl the weight while your upper arms stay in contact with the pad. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Hammer Press On Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and your back straight. Take a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing inwards and your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Incline Chest Press
description: Set the incline bench to a 45-degree angle. Take a seat on the bench with your back against the pad and feet planted. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Kickback
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in your right hand. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, with your spine steady. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Hold the upper arm beside your torso and straighten the elbow behind you. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Lateral Raise
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing your body. Keep your spine in a comfortable neutral position and your core engaged throughout the exercise. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides to about shoulder height without leaning or shrugging. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Lateral Raise With Support
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in one hand, with your palm facing your body. Set your other hand on a stable surface, such as a bench or wall, for support. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides to about shoulder height without leaning or shrugging. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Press On Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle. Take a dumbbell in one hand and position it at shoulder height, with your elbow bent and palm facing forward. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Prone Curl
description: Position yourself face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down. Extend your arm fully, letting it hang straight down toward the floor. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Prone Hammer Curl
description: Position yourself face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing your body and arm straight. Keep your upper arm stationary and curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder, contracting your biceps. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl with palms facing each other and elbows near your sides; avoid rocking back. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Pullover On Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and your knees bent at a 90-degree angle. Take a dumbbell with one hand and extend your arm straight up above your chest. Set the ribs down and keep a small elbow bend before lowering the weight. Lower the weight in an arc behind your head until you feel a comfortable shoulder stretch. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Pull the weight back over the chest along the same arc, without lifting the ribs; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Reverse Fly (With Support)
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; your back straight. Take a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing inwards. Keep a soft elbow bend and set the shoulders before moving the arms. Open your arms out and back with a slight elbow bend, drawing the shoulder blades together. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Open the arms back along the same arc without dropping the load; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Reverse Preacher Curl
description: Take a seat on a preacher bench with your chest against the pad and your arm extended over the edge of the bench, holding a dumbbell with palms facing up. Lower the dumbbell With control until your arm is straight. Set the working upper arm against the preacher pad and leave the elbow free to bend. Curl the weight while your upper arms stay in contact with the pad. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Reverse Spider Curl
description: Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing down and arm straight. With your upper arm stationary, curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder by flexing your elbow. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl the weight with your palms facing down, keeping the elbows close and torso still. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Reverse Wrist Curl
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your feet planted. Take a dumbbell in one hand with palms facing down, palm facing down. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Reverse-Grip Press
description: Take a seat on a flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing toward your body. Set your feet planted and Keep your spine in a comfortable neutral position. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Seated Biceps Curl On Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with your feet planted and your back straight. Take a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing up and your arm straight. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Seated Hammer Curl
description: Take a seat on a bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl with palms facing each other and elbows near your sides; avoid rocking back. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Seated Neutral Wrist Curl
description: Plant both feet while seated on a bench; hold a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing up. Set your forearm on your thigh, letting your wrist to hang off the edge. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Shoulder Press
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width and hold a dumbbell in one hand at shoulder level, palm facing forward. Brace your trunk and press the dumbbell straight up overhead, fully extending your arm. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Standing Curl
description: Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand, palm facing forward and arm straight. With your upper arm stationary, exhale and curl the weight upward while contracting your biceps. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Bend your elbows to bring the weight toward your shoulders without swinging your torso. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Standing Hammer Curl
description: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso. Hold your elbows near your torso and your upper arms stationary. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl with palms facing each other and elbows near your sides; avoid rocking back. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Triceps Extension (On Bench)
description: Take a seat on a bench with your back straight and feet planted. Take a dumbbell in one hand and place your other hand on the bench for support. Set the upper arms in place before extending the elbows. Keep the upper arms steady and extend through the elbows to move the weight. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Bend the elbows slowly to return to the start of the next rep; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Upright Row
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in one hand with palms facing down. Let the dumbbell hang at arm's length ahead of your thighs, with your palm facing your body. Set the torso and allow the arms to reach forward without rounding excessively. Draw your elbows back and bring the handle or weight toward your torso. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Reach the arms forward again without letting the torso lurch; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Wrist Curl
description: Take a seat on a bench or chair with your feet planted. Take a dumbbell in one hand with palms facing up, resting your forearm on your thigh. Keep the elbows relaxed so the small muscles of the hand or forearm take the load. Move through the wrists or fingers while the forearms stay supported and still. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Ease back to the start without letting the load fall from your hands; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Arm Zottman Preacher Curl
description: Take a seat on a preacher curl bench and hold a dumbbell in one hand with palms facing up. Set your upper arm on the preacher bench pad, letting your arm to fully extend. Set the working upper arm against the preacher pad and leave the elbow free to bend. Curl palms-up, turn the palms down at the top, and lower with that overhand grip. Keep both shoulders level and resist turning toward the working arm. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-Leg Fly On Exercise Ball
description: Take a seat on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other. Set one foot on the ground and extend the other leg straight out in front of you. Keep a soft elbow bend and set the shoulders before moving the arms. With a soft bend in the elbows, sweep your arms together in a wide arc. Keep the pelvis level as the supporting leg does the work. Open the arms back along the same arc without dropping the load; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Single-leg Hip Thrust
description: The single-leg hip thrust is performed by placing your upper back on a weight bench, raising one leg, and extending the hip of the other leg to achieve an isolated contraction of the glute. By working each side separately, you can fully isolate your glutes unilaterally, providing maximal training stimulus.

name: Dumbbell Squat
description: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs). Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section. Begin to slowly lower your torso by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly. Begin to raise your torso as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot mainly as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

name: Dumbbell Standing Alternate Hammer Curl and Press
description: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body. Hold your elbows near your torso and your back straight. Set the shoulders and upper arms before bending the elbows. Curl with palms facing each other and elbows near your sides; avoid rocking back. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Lower until the elbows are nearly straight, keeping the upper arms still; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Standing Alternate Overhead Press
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with your palms facing forward. Before moving, press one dumbbell overhead, fully extending your arm. Brace the torso and align the wrists with the forearms. Press the weight or handles away while keeping your trunk braced. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Lower the weight to its starting height under control before pressing again; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Standing Alternate Raise
description: Stand and set your feet about shoulder width, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body. Keep your spine in a comfortable neutral position and your core engaged. Start with a manageable load and a small bend in the elbows. Lift the weights away from your torso to about shoulder height, keeping the elbows softly bent. Finish one side's motion before the other side takes over. Lower the arms slowly to your sides without swinging the weight; switch sides when the set calls for it.

name: Dumbbell Standing Around World
description: Lay down on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms of the hands facing towards the ceiling. Tip: Your arms should be parallel to the floor and next to your thighs. To avoid injury, make sure that you keep your elbows slightly bent. This will be your starting position. Now move the dumbbells by creating a semi-circle as you displace them from the initial position to over the head. All of the movement should happen with the arms parallel to the floor at all times.
